messages.content:
Two groups of adults had systolic blood pressure measured.
Group A: n = 25, mean = 132.4 mmHg, SD = 10.2.
Group B: n = 30, mean = 126.1 mmHg, SD = 11.8.
Assuming equal variances, compute the pooled standard deviation and the 95% confidence interval for the difference in means (A minus B) using the t distribution. Give both to two decimals.
End with exactly one line: ANSWER: pooled_sd=<x>; ci=(<lo>, <hi>)

message.content:
## Pooled Standard Deviation

$$s_p^2 = \frac{(n_A-1)s_A^2 + (n_B-1)s_B^2}{n_A+n_B-2} = \frac{24(10.2^2) + 29(11.8^2)}{53}$$

$$s_p^2 = \frac{24(104.04) + 29(139.24)}{53} = \frac{2496.96 + 4037.96}{53} = \frac{6534.92}{53} = 123.30$$

$$s_p = 11.10 \text{ mmHg}$$

## Standard Error of the Difference

$$SE = s_p\sqrt{\frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{30}} = 11.10\sqrt{0.07333} = 11.10 \times 0.2708 = 3.006$$

## Confidence Interval

- Difference in means: $\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B = 132.4 - 126.1 = 6.3$
- Degrees of freedom: $df = 25 + 30 - 2 = 53$
- Critical value: $t_{0.975, 53} \approx 2.006$

$$6.3 \pm 2.006 \times 3.006 = 6.3 \pm 6.03$$

$$95\% \text{ CI: } (0.27, 12.33)$$

Since the interval excludes 0, the difference in means is statistically significant at the 5% level.

ANSWER: pooled_sd=11.10; ci=(0.27, 12.33)
